steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 2-quart baking dish.
Boil macaroni in a large pot of lightly salted water until barely cooked, about 5 minutes. Drain and set aside to cool slightly.
Whisk milk and egg together in a large bowl; stir in cheese and butter.
Place par-boiled macaroni in the prepared baking dish. Pour milk mixture over macaroni, season with salt and pepper; stir until combined. Press mixture evenly into the baking dish.
Bake, uncovered, in the preheated oven until golden brown, 30 to 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Macaroni and Cheese
raw_recipe.description: This easy mac and cheese is baked in the oven for a quick and easy meal, making this delicious casserole the perfect homemade comfort food dinner.

review.reviewBody: I loved this recipe, however I did make a couple of minor modifications. First, I used 4T of butter, and 3.5c of cheese. Second, I warmed/melted cheese into the milk/egg mixture on medium heat while cooking the macaroni. Third, I put a layer of Italian Bread Crumbs on top of dish and covered for 15 minutes while baking. Uncovered it for the last 15 minutes then stirred in the bread crumbs before serving.

I was a little wary of trying this recipe, after reading all the other reviews. But I tried it anyway cause my fiance and I love mac and cheese, this recipe turned out great it wasn't at all clumpy , to dry or anything else that I read on here. The only changes I made were I added 4 cups of mozzarella and cheddar (2cups of each) and baked it for 50 minutes (covered the first 20) I also stirred it a couple times. Thank you so much for this recipe I will definitely be making this again..

This is really good old-school macaroni, the type that basically keeps its shape when you serve it - exactly what I was looking for. I only added a few things: I stirred 1/4 tsp. creole seasoning and about 1/8 tsp. cayenne along with the salt & pepper in the milk mixture. I used a little more colby-jack cheese than noted, and reserved a little handful to top the macaroni before going into the oven. After baking for 30 minutes, I topped the macaroni with buttered Italian-style bread crumbs (almost a cup of crumbs and 2 Tbsp. melted butter) and baked the last 10 minutes. Zippier than average macaroni, but still recognizable and very comforting. Perfect!

I was a little leary of this recipe based on the other reviews. However, I needed a simple mac and cheese recipes. I took all the reviews into account and made some adjustments when I made this mac and cheese. Here are my changes: I used 22 oz of macaroni, 1/2 stick of butter, 2 cups of mozzerella cheese and 2 cups of sharp cheddar cheese. I added salt and pepper to the milk, butter, and egg mixture. I did not mix the cheese with the mixture, but layered the cheese, alternating with the macaroni. Then I poured the liquid mixture on top and laid a final layer of cheese. I covered it with aluminum foil and baked for 30 minutes. Then I removed the foil and baked for another 20 minutes. The dish turned out great!

This is similiar to the Mac n cheese my mum made when I was a child. I have been making it this way ever since. Sometimes I add shredded chicken or diced ham. I vary the cheese, always cheddar, But sometimes I mix cream cheese in, or mozzarella, goulda, whatever I have on hand. Sometimes I add hot peppers in. I always add jarred Parmesan to the top to get crispy edges. Regardless of the variations, I love this recipe. It's so easy and the custard style reminds me of mum! I use cream instead of milk. I grease an 8X11 baking dish, pour in half the noodles, cover with 1/2 the cheese, pour in the rest of the noodles, top with the rest of the cheese, pour the cream/egg mixture over the noodles and top with Parmesan cheese! No issues with anything runny or separated.

I didn't make this recipe as it is written. The recipe isn't bad, but changes need to be made. After reading other reviews about there being to much liquid, I agreed, so only used 1 1/2 cups of milk. I did add an egg, but after eating the mac and cheese, saw no point in it, so won't be adding next time. The cheese flavor wasn't what my husband and I were looking for, so next time I will use another cheese, maybe shredded mac and cheese. I melted the cheese with the milk, butter and egg. 1 1/2 cups of milk was plenty, there was not too much liquid, it all blended together very well while baking. I covered the casserole dish taking the cover off 15 min before the mac and cheese was done. I'm submitting another review on this recipe. After trial and error, trying different cheeses, etc, I finally found the perfect combination my husband I like. I heated 1 1/4 cups of milk. Once that was heated, I added three TBLs to an egg, stirring until well combined, set aside. I added 1 TBLSP butter to the milk mixture. Next I cut up 4oz each of Vermont Cheddar, Gouda and Monterey Jack cheese, Cabot brand, stirring until melted. Next, slowly add egg mixture while stirring until well combine. Next, put cooked macaroni in a casserole dish and pour mixture over that, stir well, cover and baked 350 for 30 min. The dish had great flavor and came out so creamy.

This turned out VERY tasty! To the egg/milk/ butter mixture I added garlic powder, onion powder, paprika and old bay (key ingredient, but dont add too much - a few shakes will do). I used 4T butter and 3.5 cups of cheese. I also layered noodles and cheese 3 or 4 times, ending with a cheese layer and then poured the mixture over top, per another reviewers suggestion. Salt and pepper on first 2 layers of noodles only. baked covered for 20 mins then uncovered another 20 mins. 

I will note that there were white chunky curdles all throughout the dish when I dug into it. Im guessing that's a result of adding the melted butter into the cold milk/egg mixture (I let the butter sit to cool before adding it). Is it supposed to be this way? Next time I will take another reviewer's advice and warm the egg/milk mixture on the stove then add the melted butter to the already warm mixture to see if that helps. Otherwise, the flavor was 100% restaurant /catering quality. This is the first time I made this recipe, so if someone knows how to avoid the white chunks please let me know! Will definitely make this again, and likely for holidays as well!

Love this and make it often. Note to chefs who complain about the lack of melting or clumping. Many (most?) packaged shredded cheese uses a coating to prevent the cheese from sticking together in the bag. This can interfere with achieving an even melt. For better results try shredding yourself, or precooking the cheese sauce before pouring over the macaroni.

I've had to modify the recipe. The first time I made it, the dish was very plain. So, after par-boiling the mac, I shock it with ice to prevent it from absorbing moisture. The second modification was to mix the egg, milk, cheese together and then added in the pasta. Added salt and pepper, then combined all ingredients well and poured in the square baking pan. This was definitely better than the first attempt.

I printed this recipe in 2003 when my three children were small. It is so good, I have seriously made it every single week of their lives. My oldest son recently turned 24 and asked me to make this for his birthday dinner because he loves it so much. The only change I made was to melt 1 tbsp of butter into one cup of Italian seasoned bread crumbs and sprinkle them on top during the last five minutes of baking. It is so easy and delicious! I have taken it to several potlucks and everybody always asks for the recipe! I just sent it to my daughter's best friend from elementary through high school, she remembers eating it at my house over the years and now wants to make it for her own little girl. Thank you so much for sharing this recipe so many years ago, Meredith!

This was so good both my husband and I went back at least 3 times for more. I followed some of the other reviews by layering the cheese (noodles, seasoning, cheese, repeat). Then topped with the milk, egg, butter mix. Then baked for 35 min and topped with breadcrumbs for last 5.

Great for kids. Drained macaroni, mixed milk and egg in pan, added butter to melt, then mixed in cheese and added to macaroni. Next time I will top with 1/2-3/4 c extra shredded cheese and then sprinkle with 1/2 c. panko mixed with 1 tbsp melted butter as suggested above. Spiced adults up with a a little cayenne and creole seasoning salt. Might add dry mustard if not making for children.

This first time I made it (followed the recipe) the cheese mixture rose to the top. The second time I mixed everything together in a mixing bowl then put it in the baking dish it basically came out the same. Seems like you are basically cooking the milk. Do not recommend this recipe.
Delicious! Next time, I'd stir halfway through cooking to more evenly cook the noodles.
Turned to curds and whey when i followed the recipe to the letter.

This is the Mac and cheese my mom made. She used Colby and it's very good. I recommend layering the pasta and cheese and pouring over the milk, egg and melted butter mixture . Lots of fresh ground black pepper really livens this up.

Like the recipe, baked without adding one egg. Might try in the future mixing in one egg in the ingredients provided. On the baking list to try again, but with all the ingredients required. Only gave 4 star because mine wasn't like the above! :(
Not good, not creamy! Missing flavor!

Very good! I usually make my "tried and true" baked mac that requires a roux and a lot of other extra steps and this was a perfect less time consuming recipe. I used sharp cheddar, aged white cheddar, and Monterey because that's what I had on hand. It was almost the exact same in texture and flavor. I did make a topping out of panko breadcrumbs, grated parmesan, and paprika.
Not creamy enough
